title: Renting Bikes
statementMd:
A group of $*n*$ schoolboys decided to ride bikes. As nobody of them has a bike, the boys need to rent them.

The renting site offered them $*m*$ bikes. The renting price is different for different bikes, renting the $*j*$-th bike costs $*p*_{*j*}$ rubles.

In total, the boys' shared budget is $*a*$ rubles. Besides, each of them has his own personal money, the $*i*$-th boy has $*b*_{*i*}$ personal rubles. The shared budget can be spent on any schoolchildren arbitrarily, but each boy's personal money can be spent on renting only this boy's bike.

Each boy can rent *at most one bike*, one cannot give his bike to somebody else.

What maximum number of schoolboys will be able to ride bikes? What minimum sum of personal money will they have to spend in total to let as many schoolchildren ride bikes as possible?

## Input

The first line of the input contains three integers $*n*$, $*m*$ and $*a*$ ($1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10^{5}$; $0 ≤ *a* ≤ 10^{9}$). The second line contains the sequence of integers $*b*_{1}, *b*_{2}, ..., *b*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *b*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{4}$), where $*b*_{*i*}$ is the amount of the $*i*$-th boy's personal money. The third line contains the sequence of integers $*p*_{1}, *p*_{2}, ..., *p*_{*m*}$ ($1 ≤ *p*_{*j*} ≤ 10^{9}$), where $*p*_{*j*}$ is the price for renting the $*j*$-th bike.

## Output

Print two integers $*r*$ and $*s*$, where $*r*$ is the maximum number of schoolboys that can rent a bike and $*s*$ is the minimum total personal money needed to rent $*r*$ bikes. If the schoolchildren cannot rent any bikes, then $*r* = *s* = 0$.

## Note

In the first sample both schoolchildren can rent a bike. For instance, they can split the shared budget in half (5 rubles each). In this case one of them will have to pay 1 ruble from the personal money and the other one will have to pay 2 rubles from the personal money. In total, they spend 3 rubles of their personal money. This way of distribution of money minimizes the amount of spent personal money.
statementZhMd:
一群 $*n*$ 名男学生决定骑自行车。由于他们没有人拥有自行车，因此需要租车。

租车处提供了 $*m*$ 辆自行车。不同自行车的租金不同，租用第 $*j*$ 辆自行车需要花费 $*p*_{*j*}$ 卢布。

男学生们共有 $*a*$ 卢布的公共预算。此外，每个人还有自己的私有资金，第 $*i*$ 名男学生有 $*b*_{*i*}$ 卢布。公共预算可以任意分配给任何学生使用，但每个男学生的私有资金只能用于租用他自己的自行车。

每个男学生最多只能租用一辆自行车，并且不能将自己的自行车交给其他人使用。

最多有多少名男学生能够骑上自行车？为了让尽可能多的学生骑上自行车，他们总共至少需要花费多少私有资金？

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含三个整数 $*n*$、$*m*$ 和 $*a*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10^{5}$；$0 ≤ *a* ≤ 10^{9}$）。

第二行包含整数序列 $*b*_{1}, *b*_{2}, ..., *b*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *b*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{4}$），其中 $*b*_{*i*}$ 表示第 $*i*$ 名男学生拥有的私有资金数额。

第三行包含整数序列 $*p*_{1}, *p*_{2}, ..., *p*_{*m*}$（$1 ≤ *p*_{*j*} ≤ 10^{9}$），其中 $*p*_{*j*}$ 表示租用第 $*j*$ 辆自行车的价格。

## 输出格式

输出两个整数 $*r*$ 和 $*s*$，其中 $*r*$ 是能够租到自行车的男学生的最大数量，$*s*$ 是租用 $*r*$ 辆自行车所需的最少私有资金总额。如果学生们无法租到任何自行车，则输出 $*r* = *s* = 0$。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，两名学生都可以租到自行车。例如，他们可以将公共预算平分（每人 5 卢布）。这种情况下，其中一人需要用 1 卢布私有资金支付，另一人需要用 2 卢布私有资金支付。他们总共花费了 3 卢布的私有资金。这样的资金分配方式使私有资金的花费总额最少。
